source_solver: OR-Tools 9.15.6755 CP-SAT; original example single_machine_scheduling_with_setup_release_due_dates_sat.py (stable branch) run unmodified with its default flags (num_search_workers:16, max_time_in_seconds:45, preprocess_times true) in a subprocess on 2026-11-02 (status OPTIMAL, best bound 112605, 0.04 s)
notes: Objective is the makespan (the original minimises max end time; due dates are hard deadlines, -1 = none). Original CP-SAT model: 15 starts + 15 ends + 240 circuit literals (15 from the dummy node, 15 to it, 210 job-to-job) + makespan = 271 variables; 15 intervals + 1 NoOverlap + 15 enforced 'first job' rows + 210 enforced setup rows + 1 Circuit + 2 precedences + 1 LinMax = 245 constraints. The PuLP port is a MILP with different sizes. AddCircuit becomes an assignment structure over the empty-machine node: follows[from_job, to_job] binaries (start->job 15, job->job 210, job->end 15 = 240), one in- and one out-row per job plus first/last rows (32). The enforced setup rows become a time-flow (arc-time) formulation: handover[i, j] = end of i if j directly follows i (225 continuous), handover_out (sum over arcs = end, 15), sequence (start_j >= sum_i handover[i, j] + setup[i, j] * follows[i, j], 15), handover_max/min (450, bounded by deadlines, earliest end, follows) and makespan = sum of handovers into 'end' (1); positive durations break sub-tours. The plain big-M port (start_j >= end_i + setup - M(1 - follows)) reproduces 112605 but no open solver proves it within 60 s (HiGHS 118951, SCIP 117072, CBC 120978 incumbents at the limit), so the port adds valid strengthening not in the original: runs_before[i, j] binaries for i < j (105), follows <= before (210), big-M 'before' rows start_j >= end_i + least job-to-job setup into j (210), head_j (start >= jobs before it + their least incoming setups) and tail_j (makespan >= end_j + jobs after it + their least job-to-job setups) (30). Precedences 2, duration rows 15. Port: 240 + 105 = 345 binaries, 15 + 15 + 225 + 1 = 256 continuous = 601 variables; 32 + 15 + 15 + 15 + 450 + 1 + 210 + 210 + 30 + 2 = 980 rows. The big-M of a before row is due[i] + least setup into j - earliest start of j (due = horizon when there is no deadline; horizon = sum of durations + sum of each job's largest incoming setup, as in the original) - structural, computed from the data. The original's 'start == end + setup when release is 0' equalities and 'start == max(release, initial setup) if first' become >= (left-shifting a schedule never raises the makespan); its preprocess_times step (moving the least incoming setup into the duration) is an equivalent transformation and is not ported. setup_times keeps the 15 x 15 off-diagonal entries plus the 15 initial setups; the 15 diagonal entries of the original matrix are unused by its model and are dropped. HiGHS 112605 (1.1 s), SCIP 112605 (5.7 s), CBC 112605 (5.9 s). Alternative optima: makespan is unique by definition; over plans with makespan 112605 (HiGHS min/max) total_setup_time ranges 26504..27856 (total_idle_time accordingly), min_deadline_slack 0..1, first_job job_1 or job_5; last_job is job_13 in every optimal plan but is not scored (a plan identity that can tie in scenarios). SCORING_KPIS = makespan.
